html:
Osaka is a great port city at the mouth of the Yodo River on Osaka Bay, in the Kansai region of Japan. For centuries it was the country's commercial capital.

As Naniwa, it was a port and at times a capital of the early Japanese state, the gateway for envoys and ideas from Korea and China. In the 1500s it was the stronghold of a militant Buddhist sect, which held out for ten years against Oda Nobunaga. On that site Toyotomi Hideyoshi built Osaka Castle from 1583. The Tokugawa destroyed his heirs there in the sieges of 1614 and 1615.

In Tokugawa Japan Osaka was called "the kitchen of the nation". Lords sold their tax rice there, merchants shipped goods to Edo, and the Dōjima Rice Exchange traded rice futures from 1697. Its townsmen supported puppet theatre and kabuki. In the Tenmei famine of the 1780s its poor rioted against rice dealers.

In the 1900s it became an industrial city. Kōnosuke Matsushita founded what became Panasonic there in 1918, and instant noodles were invented nearby in 1958.
sum: Osaka is a great port city at the mouth of the Yodo River on Osaka Bay, in the Kansai region of Japan. For centuries it was the country's commercial capital.
